:::{#exm-binomial-not}
#### Draws without replacement are not binomial

An urn holds two red balls and two blue balls.
Draw two balls without replacement,
and let $X$ be the number of red balls drawn.
Each draw is red with probability $1/2$,
but $X \not\sim \dBinf{2, 1/2}$,
because the draws are not [independent](independence.qmd#def-indpt):

$$
\ba
\P(X = 2)
&= \P(\text{first red}) \cd \P(\text{second red} \mid \text{first red})
&& \text{(multiplication rule)} \\
&= \frac{2}{4} \cd \frac{1}{3}
&& \text{(one red ball is left among three)} \\
&= \frac{1}{6}
&& \text{(multiply)}
\ea
$$

whereas, by @eq-binom-pmf, a $\dBinf{2, 1/2}$ random variable has

$$
\ba
\P(X = 2)
&= \binom{2}{2} \paren{\frac{1}{2}}^2 \paren{\frac{1}{2}}^0
&& \text{(binomial PMF with } n = 2,\ \prob = 1/2,\ x = 2 \text{)} \\
&= \frac{1}{4}
&& \text{(evaluate)}
\ea
$$

:::
